proposal.policy_prompt_for_action:
The failures occurred during initial button localization, immediately after the approach reached its approximate hover, and near the scheduled descent time. The retained motion_reference correctly preserved the initial motion and absolute timing; its updates agreed with the memory instruction. These are action-rule SUFFICIENCY failures, not missing historical facts or memory PREDICTABILITY failures.

Replace the tabletop-projection localization guidance with calibrated two-view localization. Identify the same gray circular button-center feature in the current front and wrist images. Construct its world-space rays using each camera's intrinsics and extrinsics, and estimate their closest intersection. Use that point's xy for the button center, accounting for the button's elevation rather than intersecting the top-center ray with the tabletop. Cross-check against the white base. Use this button-centered xy for hover, press and retraction; do not substitute the achieved hover TCP. For example, a button near (-0.186, -0.174) m should not acquire the approximately centimetre-scale bias caused by projecting its raised top onto the table. When the button is occluded, use the retained unobstructed reference images with the fixed front calibration.

Clarify the hover-entry condition. A TCP at approximately z=0.15 m, within about 0.02 m horizontally of the localized button center, is already at the timing hover. The observed approach errors of roughly 0.013–0.016 m do not mean alignment is lost. Once in this region, apply the scheduled wait or press rule; do not insert another hover waypoint merely to refine xy or close visibly open fingers. A wait preserves the current gripper state. Keep the initial approach, press and retraction commands at gripper -1, but remove any implication that a closed-gripper requirement authorizes an extra closing motion during the timing wait. Reserve hover realignment for genuinely larger errors or an unsafe pose.

Retain the period reconstruction and ordinal-passage formula T_N=P/4+(N-1)P/2, but replace the assertion that a 20-step lead is sufficient everywhere except at far-right buttons. The recorded successful descents establish geometry-dependent effective leads, not a universal dependence on y alone. Use the following local button-geometry calibration anchors for a hover near z=0.15 m and a button-centered press command at z=0.0075 m: near xy=(-0.163, -0.007) m, use L=22 steps; near (-0.233, -0.013) m, use L=24; near (-0.193, 0.095) m, use L=25. Retain the 20-step nominal lead for the right-side geometry near (-0.200, -0.160) m and near (-0.186, -0.174) m, and the previously specified approximately 22-step calibration near the farther-right y=-0.19 m geometry. These are local spatial calibration anchors, not choices based on cube color or requested ordinal. Do not claim that these observations establish an exact lead model for arbitrary button locations.

Compute S=T_N-L from the measured period and applicable geometry calibration. When hovering, press immediately if t>=S-1; otherwise wait min(30, round(S-t)) steps. This one-step execution tolerance prevents a needless one-step wait when the actual elapsed time has reached just before nominal S. Always use the reported absolute elapsed_control_steps, not a sum of requested waits. The calibrated examples imply a fifth passage at 540 with descent starting at 518, a fourth passage at 420 with descent starting at 396, and a second passage at 180 with descent starting at 155. Thus at t=138 in the latter situation the remaining wait is 17, not 22. A fourth passage at 280 permits immediate descent at t=259 under the one-step tolerance, while a fifth passage at 360 with L=20 retains the scheduled start at 340. Remove the unconditional example claiming that every fourth passage with P=240 starts at 400; that result applies only when the applicable lead is 20.

Keep the existing button-centered press waypoint, contact-limited-height distinction, retraction after contact, and prohibition on identical-pose waypoints. No memory field needs to be added or changed: the retained initial frames and current calibrated observations provide the timing and geometry needed for these corrected rules.
proposal.refused: Do not carry forward the early-hover report's conclusion that the second passage with P=240 must use press start 160. That conclusion merely repeats the old 20-step default; the later recorded wait and descent for the same button geometry establish start 155 and an effective 25-step lead. Also do not turn the individual lead corrections into a claimed universal geometric or motion-duration formula. The supplied trajectories support local calibration anchors, but do not identify such a formula. Their full descent durations include motion after button activation and cannot simply be substituted for the effective pre-passage lead. The shared hover, localization and timing failures are otherwise passed on.

policy_prompt_for_action.modify_from: Infer the button's world xy from the calibrated images and its tabletop base, using the wrist view to refine localization.
policy_prompt_for_action.modify_to: Identify the same gray circular button-center feature in the current front and wrist images. Using each camera's intrinsics and world-to-camera extrinsics, construct world-space rays through that feature and estimate their closest intersection. Use the resulting point's xy as the button center, cross-checking against the white base. Account for the raised button top; do not intersect its center ray with the tabletop plane. Use this localized button-centered xy for approach, press and retraction.

policy_prompt_for_action.modify_from: While hovering approximately 0.15 m above the button, keep the gripper closed and determine when to press.
policy_prompt_for_action.modify_to: A TCP at approximately z=0.15 m and within about 0.02 m horizontally of the localized button center is already at the timing hover. In this region determine when to press using the timing rules below; do not insert another hover waypoint to refine xy or close visibly open fingers. Waits preserve the current gripper state. Keep gripper command -1 for the initial approach, press and retraction.

policy_prompt_for_action.modify_from: Begin the downward press about 20 control steps before the requested target passage. Thus compute the press-start step S = P/4 + (N-1)P/2 - L. Use L = 20 steps normally; use approximately 22 steps for a button toward the robot's far right, near y = -0.19 m, where the demonstrated descent needs slightly more lead. This gives press starts of 400 for the fourth passage with P=240, 280 for the third with P=240, 190 for the fourth with P=120, approximately 178 for the third with P=160 at the far-right button, and 340 for the fifth with P=160. These are consequences of measured periods and button geometry, not episode identifiers.
policy_prompt_for_action.modify_to: Compute the requested passage time T_N = P/4 + (N-1)P/2 and press-start step S = T_N - L. L is the effective lead to button activation, not the full descent duration, and depends on button geometry rather than y alone. For a hover near z=0.15 m and a button-centered press command at z=0.0075 m, use these local spatial calibration anchors: near button xy=(-0.163, -0.007) m, L=22 steps; near (-0.233, -0.013) m, L=24; near (-0.193, 0.095) m, L=25; near (-0.200, -0.160) m or (-0.186, -0.174) m, L=20; for the farther-right geometry near y=-0.19 m, L approximately 22. Select an applicable local calibration from the localized button geometry, never from cube color or requested ordinal. Away from these calibrated neighborhoods, 20 steps is only a nominal estimate; these anchors do not establish an exact lead formula for arbitrary locations. Do not substitute total descent duration for L.

policy_prompt_for_action.modify_from: If the current step t is below S, wait min(30, round(S-t)) control steps in place, maintaining the closed gripper. Do not take an extra full 30-step wait when fewer steps remain. If t has reached S and the hand is still hovering, command [button_x, button_y, 0.0075, -3.1416, 0, 0] with gripper command -1.
policy_prompt_for_action.modify_to: Use the reported absolute elapsed_control_steps as t, not a sum of requested waits. If the hand is at the timing hover and t>=S-1, command [button_x, button_y, 0.0075, -3.1416, 0, 0] with gripper command -1 immediately. Otherwise, while hovering with t<S-1, wait min(30, round(S-t)) control steps in place, preserving the current gripper state. Do not take an extra full 30-step wait when fewer steps remain, or a needless one-step wait within the press-start tolerance.

policy_prompt_for_action.modify_from: If the button is temporarily occluded, recover its position from the retained unobstructed frames. If alignment is genuinely lost, move to the safe button-centered hover before attempting contact.
policy_prompt_for_action.modify_to: If the button is temporarily occluded, recover its position from retained unobstructed reference images using the fixed front-camera calibration and the button's raised geometry rather than projecting its top onto the table. Reserve a corrective button-centered hover for horizontal errors genuinely larger than the approximately 0.02 m timing-hover tolerance or an unsafe pose. An achieved hover offset within that tolerance does not require realignment; use the button center, not the achieved TCP xy, for the subsequent press.

The proposed second-passage start of 160 for the geometry requiring a 25-step lead is not committed.

fields.name: motion_reference
fields.description: With empty memory write [E0]. If the incoming list contains only E0 and this cycle shows that execution time has advanced, append all displayed execution front-camera labels in chronological order, excluding duplicates. Otherwise carry the incoming list unchanged. A zero-step action does not trigger appending. Once the initial motion frames have been appended, never append further frames or replace the list. Use the stored images and their absolute step labels as the reference for reconstructing the cube's periodic motion. e.g. ["E0", "E1", "E17", "E33", "E46"]
fields.annotation: An ordered list of execution keyframes documenting the initial cube motion. At the first cycle write [E0]. At the first cycle showing actual elapsed motion, append that cycle's displayed front-camera frame labels in chronological order, excluding duplicates. Freeze this list thereafter. These frames preserve the initial endpoint, early motion and its absolute timing, allowing the oscillation period and numbered future target passages to be inferred even when later images show the same positions again. They also retain the unobstructed button location. Do not select frames from future cycles. e.g. ["E0", "E1", "E17", "E33", "E46"]

texts.action:
Start by locating the gray circular button on its white base, the colored moving cube, and the purple target. Identify the same gray circular button-center feature in the current front and wrist images. Using each camera's intrinsics and world-to-camera extrinsics, construct world-space rays through that feature and estimate their closest intersection. Use the resulting point's xy as the button center, cross-checking against the white base. Account for the raised button top; do not intersect its center ray with the tabletop plane. Use this localized button-centered xy for approach, press and retraction. Do not use image left/right as robot left/right. When the TCP is initially high and has not approached the button, command [button_x, button_y, 0.15, -3.1416, 0, 0] with gripper command -1. Use the button center, not the slightly displaced achieved hover TCP, for subsequent commanded xy.

A TCP at approximately z=0.15 m and within about 0.02 m horizontally of the localized button center is already at the timing hover. In this region determine when to press using the timing rules below; do not insert another hover waypoint to refine xy or close visibly open fingers. Waits preserve the current gripper state. Keep gripper command -1 for the initial approach, press and retraction. Read the requested ordinal N from the goal. Use motion_reference together with the current motion frames and absolute elapsed_control_steps to reconstruct the cube's oscillation. The cube starts at one endpoint and moves smoothly back and forth; count a passage through the target in either direction, not a complete round trip. Fit the motion in world tabletop coordinates rather than assuming constant image velocity. In these trajectories the target is the midpoint of the oscillation: for full period P, passage times are P/4 + (N-1)P/2. Infer P from observed motion, not from the requested ordinal or the cube's color. The demonstrated periods include 120, 160 and 240 control steps. Initial and current frames should agree with the inferred phase; do not reset the passage count when the cube returns to an earlier-looking position.

Compute the requested passage time T_N = P/4 + (N-1)P/2 and press-start step S = T_N - L. L is the effective lead to button activation, not the full descent duration, and depends on button geometry rather than y alone. For a hover near z=0.15 m and a button-centered press command at z=0.0075 m, use these local spatial calibration anchors: near button xy=(-0.163, -0.007) m, L=22 steps; near (-0.233, -0.013) m, L=24; near (-0.193, 0.095) m, L=25; near (-0.200, -0.160) m or (-0.186, -0.174) m, L=20; for the farther-right geometry near y=-0.19 m, L approximately 22.
